clips.title: Zuck's AI corner coach
clips.hook: Mark has cameras in his gym and his agent coaches him between MMA rounds
clips.why: Zuck + MMA + AI is a pattern interrupt on any feed. Concrete, visual, funny ('you took 30 seconds, I only have 60'), and it lands on a big idea: everyone will write code without knowing it.

clips.title: Writing a $100B check before seeing the model
clips.hook: 'Alex, are you sure this is going to work?'
clips.why: The episode's own cold open, for a reason: a giant number, real stakes, and a CFO pulling the AI chief aside to say failure would be 'really, really bad'. Tension with a clear landing.

clips.title: Why Zuck bet on Alexandr Wang
clips.hook: 'The social media guy working with the data guy?'
clips.why: Founder-on-founder conviction with a quotable, uncensored landing line. Addresses the skeptic's question head on, plus a laugh from the host's 'eighth wonder of the world' jab.

clips.title: 'Oh no, I've joined the wrong company'
clips.hook: A lead told Alex they didn't need a reasoning model
clips.why: Story structure in under a minute: setup, a shocking quote, a gut-punch reaction, then the turn (the CEO gets AI-pilled and the company follows). Insider drama people share.

clips.title: 4 things most CEOs wouldn't have done
clips.hook: John lists four moves other founder CEOs wouldn't make
clips.why: A numbered list is the most retention-friendly format there is: viewers stay to hear all four. It's a sharp outside read on Zuck's playbook (reboot the team, pay up, bet on potential, clear the calendar).

clips.title: The watermelon
clips.hook: Zuck's agent shops for baking day with his 3-year-old
clips.why: Wholesome, human, and tied to a known meme (the livestream watermelon). It shows the product working without sounding like an ad.

clips.title: Is that Instacart account for me or for my agent?
clips.hook: Mark became an Instacart customer only because his agent needed one
clips.why: A counterintuitive business insight: agents don't just convert better, they create new customers. Short, clean, quotable for founder and e-commerce audiences.

clips.title: Don't outsource product thinking to a PhD student
clips.hook: Are AI benchmarks actually any good?
clips.why: A spicy, quotable take on benchmaxxing from people who train frontier models. AI Twitter loves this debate, and the 'PhD student who made a viral benchmark' line will travel.

clips.title: What it costs to train a frontier model
clips.hook: 'Tens of billions of dollars is a good estimate'
clips.why: Hard numbers from someone who signs the checks ($15B a year to run a gigawatt, $50-60B to build one). Number-led clips get saved and shared.

clips.title: Burn the boats
clips.hook: Some execs wanted to be more conservative. Zuck didn't.
clips.why: Conviction plus profanity plus a reframe: 'for it not to work out, AI overall has to fail.' The emotional arc and the logic land together.

clips.title: Why Lean Startup doesn't work in AI
clips.hook: How do you build when the feedback loop is a year long?
clips.why: It challenges a sacred startup doctrine ('entrepreneurship on hard mode'). Founder-audience gold, and the question works as a hook.

clips.title: A team of insecure overachievers
clips.hook: Ask them where they'll be in 3 months: 'it's awful, we're screwed'
clips.why: A funny, relatable management trick (record the pessimism, replay it after you ship). Anyone who has worked with high performers will tag a coworker.

clips.title: AI model names are egregious
clips.hook: 'The numbers go backwards?'
clips.why: A relatable gripe everybody has, from the people making a competing product. Quick, funny, and it explains a design choice (no model picker).

clips.title: Meta ran out of fruit names
clips.hook: Avocado, Watermelon... and nobody wants Durian
clips.why: Pure banter with real laughter, and insider codenames people love to learn. A light palate cleanser between the heavier clips.

clips.title: Zuck on Alex's 'deranged' tweets
clips.hook: 'What do you make of Alex's deranged posting?'
clips.why: The host asks the question everyone wants to ask. Zuck's 'be authentic' answer and his admission that Alex's posts crack him up make it human and shareable.

clips.title: AI shouldn't lecture you
clips.hook: 'You don't want a moralizing lecture for asking it to do the thing'
clips.why: A clear, opinionated stance on alignment that sets Meta apart from other labs. It plays into an argument people already love having about preachy chatbots, so the comments will fill up.

clips.title: How college students actually use AI
clips.hook: They word-vomit for 15 minutes and let AI organise it
clips.why: A surprising, specific observation about Gen Z behaviour. Students will recognise themselves and everyone else will be curious. Short and self-contained.

clips.title: The memo Alex sent Zuck 2 days after their first call
clips.hook: A 44-minute call, then 'here's what I'd do in your position'
clips.why: An origin story with a lesson (talent density over headcount). The 'that's how they get you' banter gives it warmth, and founders save hiring advice.

clips.title: No non-technical managers
clips.hook: The point of 200 direct reports is no non-technical managers
clips.why: A contrarian org-design principle with a crisp warning: leaders lose technical touch faster than they think. Engineers will share it with their managers.

clips.title: 'We're not an app company'
clips.hook: Zuck: Meta is a deep technology company, 'just us and ByteDance' at this scale
clips.why: A bold identity claim with a competitor name-drop. It reframes how people see Meta in one breath.

clips.title: Superintelligence is for invention, not automation
clips.hook: Everyone else is obsessed with automating knowledge work
clips.why: A vision statement that takes a swipe at the rest of the industry. It reads like a thesis and gets quote-tweeted.

clips.title: 'Mark is very Bayesian'
clips.hook: Alex's review of Zuck as a boss
clips.why: Genuine praise, a nerdy compliment, and real laughter ('what lovely priors you have'). The banter makes it rewatchable.

clips.title: Telling Stripe it was behind, 3 years early
clips.hook: Alex told Patrick Collison in 2023 that agents would be buying things
clips.why: A prediction-came-true story that John can confirm on camera ('only started going vertical in September'). Credibility plus a little roast of the host's company.

clips.title: AI researchers use actual protractors
clips.hook: Frontier AI research runs on vibes and protractors held up to the monitor
clips.why: A funny, humanising behind-the-scenes detail, and it ends with a satisfying payoff (the new model beat the old one 'immediately').

clips.title: Muse Wonder... Full
clips.hook: 'You're clearly a father. This is an excellent dad joke.'
clips.why: A 15-20 second laugh, ideal as a loopable micro-short. Light, and it puts the product name in the joke.
